## 3. Base rates
- **Coin-flip model (each team wins each game 50%):** 2-2 is 37.5%, 3-1 is 50%, 4-0 is 12.5%. If one team is stronger, 2-2 becomes less likely and 3-1 and 4-0 more likely.
- **One subagent's own count of 2000-2025 series** (built from memory, not checked against box scores, so treat as uncertain; I spot-checked the 2025 entries and they are correct):

| Series (26 each) | 4-0 | 2-2 | 3-1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ALCS | 4 (15%) | 6 (23%) | 16 (62%) |
| NLCS | 4 (15%) | 6 (23%) | 16 (62%) |
| LCS combined (52) | 15% | 23% | 62% |
| World Series | 4 (15%) | 10 (38%) | 12 (46%) |

  - ALCS sweeps were 2006, 2012, 2014 and 2022.
  - ALCS series tied 2-2 were 2003, 2013, 2017, 2021, 2023 and 2025.
  - With only 26 series per group, each figure is uncertain by roughly ±9 points.
- **Published counts:**
  - About 11 LCS sweeps in roughly 80 LCS from 1985-2025, about 14%. Source: https://www.mlb.com/news/every-sweep-in-lcs-history, which covers through 2019; 2022 HOU and 2025 LAD were added by the subagent.
  - CBS (2023): 93 best-of-seven series reached 3-1. Source: https://www.cbssports.com/mlb/news/world-series-history-of-3-1-comebacks-as-diamondbacks-try-to-add-name-to-short-list-vs-rangers/
  - MLB.com: 68 best-of-seven series were tied 2-2. Source: https://www.mlb.com/news/breaking-down-importance-of-game-5-in-2-2-set-c258889428
  - Leaving out sweeps, that is roughly 58:42 for 3-1 over 2-2. This is approximate because the two counts come from different years.

criterios:
This question concerns the games won by each team in the 2026 Major League Baseball American League Championship Series (ALCS) once four games have been played (Game 4 is scheduled for Friday, October 16, 2026). It resolves according to the series score after Game 4:

- "Tied 2-2" — each team has won exactly two of the first four games.
- "One team leads 3-1" — one team has won three of the first four games (and the series continues).
- "A team completes a 4-0 sweep" — one team has won all four games, ending the series.

Resolution is based on the official 2026 ALCS results published on MLB.com's postseason page (https://www.mlb.com/postseason) or by other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
letra_pequena: The ALCS is a best-of-seven series. "After Game 4" refers to the series score once four games have been completed, regardless of the calendar date on which the fourth game is ultimately played (e.g., if games are postponed by weather). The three listed options are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive of all possible series scores once four games have been played (2-2, 3-1, or 4-0 for one side).

- 2-2: about 36%
- 3-1: about 50%

(c) **Base rates:**
- A pure coin flip gives 37.5% / 50% / 12.5%.
- The rough LCS tally for 2000–2025 gives 23% (2-2), 62% (3-1) and 15% (4-0). This comes from about 26 series per league, so each figure is uncertain by roughly ±9 points.
- Long-run counts of best-of-seven series put 3-1 ahead of 2-2 by about 58:42 when sweeps are excluded.
- LCS sweeps run about 14–15% historically.

History shows more lopsided series than a coin-flip model predicts, so I shade 3-1 above 50% and 2-2 below 36%.

- The Yankees or Guardians come back in the ALDS, producing a different and more evenly matched series that is likelier to be tied 2-2.
- Alternatively, the Rays' pitching dominance seen against the Yankees, who scored 2 runs in 18 innings, carries over and they sweep a White Sox team that won 14 fewer games.
